staticConclusions: BrowserProcessImpl eagerly initializes the default-enabled macOS KeychainKeyProvider during process startup; an incognito page does not suppress process initialization
The two-argument BASE_FEATURE macro registers kUseKeychainKeyProvider as UseKeychainKeyProvider; the installed matching CEF framework contains this feature name
Disabling the feature leaves no macOS provider in this configuration; OSCryptAsync immediately produces an empty Encryptor whose missing-key encrypt/decrypt operations return failure
The exact Chromium 154 os_crypt source directory contains async, browser and common, with no sync directory; the examined Encryptor path has no synchronous OSCrypt Keychain fallback
The historical AES empty-key decryption retry is local cryptography and performs no Keychain I/O
Off-the-record profile network storage is in memory; persistent-cookie encryption uses OSCryptAsync
The matching CEF chrome_runtime patch retains BrowserProcessImpl startup and its patch registry has no os_crypt patch; older master-branch Keychain patches are not evidence for this binary
Playwright P1 uses a different engine path whose driver includes use-mock-keychain; its successful launch does not accept CEF startup safety
isolatedTrialPrerequisites: Root separately authorizes the technical owner to execute the bounded trial after the reviewed native policy is compiled against the declared CEF version
The effective browser-process startup configuration contains the disabled UseKeychainKeyProvider before initialization; arbitrary Chromium argv remain disabled
Use a fresh owned temporary root with restrictive directory permissions and only a local isolated fixture, retaining the OS renderer sandbox and existing HTML permission boundary

Run a short single startup/load/close trial with owned-process cleanup; credential prompts make the trial fail and terminate owned workers without interacting with the prompt or changing Keychain or OS settings
Record startup policy, actual version, visual/window state and owned-worker shutdown; keep runtime safety pending until these observations pass
